hypotheses.H0: the as-built walk is not an acceptable fallback: s(as-built) < 1 (predicted 10/28 by -p1-ml.md F4, a prediction not a result)
hypotheses.H1: some candidate walk lists every dev flow item (s = 28/28)
hypotheses.note: FR-8: an impact that cannot be proven must be listed as possible; an unlisted item is a silent omission

statistic.s: per walk: the share of the 28 items that are listed. An item is listed iff Walk.items() for its anchor (column impact, bound 2) contains an item whose identity equals the item's impactedId (the dev file's impacted symbol); an item reached only as a different (kind, node) pair is not listed. The anchor is never an item. Measured through Walk.items(), not through documents (D2 of docs/reviews/connected-code-graph-p1-39b.md)
statistic.reportedBy: pooled; by language; by signature; per anchor cluster (listed clusters of 4 shown beside, because the 28 items are not independent); the ids (itemId) of every unlisted item, per walk
statistic.interval: Wilson score, 95%, on the pooled s (28/28 gives 0.879); beside it the cluster-level figure, the share of the 4 anchor clusters with every item listed (4/4 gives Wilson lower bound 0.510), because the 28 items are not independent; no interval is claimed on language or signature cells
statistic.burden: per dev anchor, per walk: the number of items Walk.items() returns for that anchor (all listed items, not only the dev items); dev burden = the sum over the 4 anchors; per-anchor values and their maximum are reported beside the sum

mustEmitBesideS.setUnionLowerBound: s of the set union of the V-flow listed set and the V-both listed set, with the item ids; a lower bound on V-union, not used by the rule
mustEmitBesideS.secondLevelCalleeOnly: for V-both and V-union: the items listed only through a second-level callee hop (callee at call depth 2), by id and with the walk's chain; not used by the rule
alsoRequired: V-union listed set is a superset of the set union (asserted; a violation is a tool defect, reported and the run voided)

the as-built result compared to the prediction from the dev hop kinds, by the record's own cut (impacted file): pooled 10/28; python 6/9; TS/JS 4/19 (the 10 pure return-use chains; -p1-ml.md F4's 6/8 and 4/20 are the anchor-language cut and are not the comparison); the one counting:true item (callee-arg,link) and the one link hop are in the 28 and in the by-signature cut as the file gives them

rule.ship: the walk with the lowest dev burden among those with the maximum s (-p1-ml.md §3.5)
rule.safeClaim: 'safe' only at n/n; 28/28 is a screen, with Wilson lower bound 0.879 (28/(28+1.96^2)), and 0.510 at the cluster level. In-sample: V-flow and V-both were designed after the dev chains' hop kinds were known (F4 derives from them), so a 28/28 on these items is not validation; the pick is validated on held-out only at the AC-5 gate, outside this record
rule.noWalkAtNN: if no walk reaches 28/28, the residual misses are recorded by signature, reported not closed; the choice by the same rule is then a screen, not a safety claim, and FR-8 is not claimed met for the residual signatures
rule.tieBreakFixedHere: before any data: if two max-s walks tie on the dev-burden sum, the lower maximum per-anchor burden wins; if still tied, the first in this fixed list wins: as-built, V-both, V-flow, V-union (ascending row count of ccg.engine.flow.candidate_table at the pinned engine: 49, 53, 62, 66). The plan does not say how 'dev burden' aggregates over the 4 anchors or how a tie resolves; these choices are the method owner's, fixed here, disclosed
rule.notUsed: the set-union lower bound, the second-level-callee-only items, and the language/signature breakdowns do not enter the rule
rule.afterwards: the pick is the input to P1-23's shipped table and its algorithm.version bump (spec2 §1.2); a shipped table other than spec2 §5's requires spec2 §5 revised by its owner before it ships; AC-25's control half closes on P1-42's fixture only if V-flow or V-union ships (-p1-ml.md §3.5)

thresholds: none beyond those ratified in -p1-ml.md §3.5: n/n for 'safe'; Wilson lower bound 0.879 at 28/28; depth bound 2. No new threshold is introduced by this record

tool.contract: Two phases with a stop between them. Phase A (build): refuse a non-throwaway port; verify the refuse-list below; build and load the snapshot as pins.corpusAndBuilder.build says; print, with no walk run and no result file, the Snapshot commit, the per-unit built commits, the loaded graph's content digest, the toolchain image id and the falkordb image digest; stop. The implementer then appends the companion line ccg-p1-flow-fallback-v1-snapshot (append-only, never edited) pinning those, and commits it. Phase B (measure): refuses unless the live graph's digest, Snapshot commit and unit commits equal that committed line; per candidate table runs ccg.engine.bfs.walk(reader, Node('Symbol', anchorId), column=impact, table=candidate_table(name)) over CypherReader for each of the 4 dev anchors and takes Walk.items(); a dev item is listed iff some Item has kind == 'symbol' and id == impactedId; a missing anchor or impacted node in the snapshot is an error, never an unlisted cluster or item. Emits one JSON (candidates, per-walk s, listed and unlisted ids, pooled/language/signature/anchor cuts, burden per anchor, sum and max, set-union lower bound, second-level-callee-only items, Wilson intervals, the as-built comparison above, the environment block); each walk run twice, byte-equal else the run is void; the tool creates cpg/eval/results/ and writes there only. Read-only on the graph; never opens ~/.local/share/ccg-eval, ~/.config/ccg, :6379 or :6390.
tool.refuseList: both phases refuse to run if any of these differs from this record: the dev file, every engine file, builderFiles, the flag registry, the three plans, cpg/tests/test_engine_bfs_rows.py, cpg/eval/EVAL_COMMIT (sha256 against the pin; a one-byte change must refuse); and if the -tool line (phase A) / the -tool and -snapshot lines (phase B) are not in the committed blob `git show HEAD:cpg/eval/preregistration.jsonl` with the file's sha256 equal to the line's, an uncommitted line does not count. The tool's own test plants one input per refusal (one changed byte in an engine file, a builder file, the dev file, a plan; a mismatched -tool sha; an uncommitted -tool line; a non-throwaway port; a dev id absent from the graph; a changed graph digest between phases) and each must exit non-zero before any walk
